title: Unified async windowed iterators for embeddings and rerank SDK samples
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a cross-language helper that exposes an ergonomic async/windowed iterator for batching and paginating embedding + rerank calls. Goals: 1) API parity for Python/TypeScript/Go so examples and best-practices can be copy/pasted between languages. 2) Built-in windowing to emit batches sized for cost/throughput targets while preserving per-item ordering for reranking workflows. 3) Backpressure-friendly streaming so callers can consume incremental results without blocking the serving runtime. 4) Integrated retry/backoff strategy for transient HTTP/gRPC failures and partial-batch errors. 5) Comprehensive examples and tests (unit + small integration) and a short migration guide for existing SDK customers.
acceptance_criteria: Language parity: same high-level API surface in Python/TS/Go with idiomatic bindings
Windowing: helper can produce fixed-size and time-windowed batches with configurable overlap=0..N
Streaming: consumer can iterate partial results as soon as a batch responds; iterator resumes correctly on transient errors
Retry/backoff: per-batch retries with jittered exponential backoff + optional idempotency token for server-side de-dup
Docs & samples: PNG-free quickstart snippets for each language + cookbook for reranking at scale

python_snippet:
# Python usage example
async def produce_inputs():
    for text in ['q1','q2','q3','q4']:
        yield text

# windowed_iter returns an async iterator that yields per-item streamed results while batching under the hood
async for result in windowed_iter(produce_inputs(), batch_size=4, max_latency_ms=100):
    # result = { 'id': str, 'embedding': [float], 'score': float (if rerank mode) }
    print(result)
tradeoffs: Windowing adds configurable latency (max_latency_ms) to allow batching; we chose conservative defaults to keep developer surprise low. Preserving strict item ordering increases implementation complexity and can hurt throughput; we provide preserve_order=false option to trade order for latency. Per-batch retry semantics are simpler but can duplicate work for non-idempotent rerank endpoints; we provide idempotency tokens and opt-in de-dup guidance in docs.
